entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will process your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

- **Verdict:** all findings addressed / findings still open.

input.message:
Task 5 fix round 1 — two findings. Fix both, then re-verify and append a fix report.

FINDING 1 (Important) — ASCII convention broken in the markdown.
`docs/kullanim-kosullari.md:90` contains `araçtir`. The `ç` is non-ASCII, and this file must stay ASCII in its body to match its sibling `docs/gizlilik-metni.md`.

Fix: `araçtir` -> `aractir`.

Then prove there are no others. Do NOT check this by eye — your own self-review said "checked visually, no ç/ğ/ı/ö/ş/ü characters" and that claim was wrong; a single grep found this immediately. Run:

    grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7F]' docs/kullanim-kosullari.md

Everything it reports from the body onward must be fixed. Note: the file may legitimately have accented text in a "Veri sorumlusu"-style header block if it has one — check what `docs/gizlilik-metni.md` does and follow the same rule. Put the grep command and its output in your fix report.

FINDING 2 (Important — I am raising this above the reviewer's "Minor") — an unrequested promise.
`site/src/pages/kosullar.astro:69` and `docs/kullanim-kosullari.md:85` say the app "onu başka bir amaçla kullanmaz" / equivalent.

Neither the brief's table nor any decision in this project authorises that commitment. The brief asked only that the user owns their content and grants the app permission to display it. This is a legal document: a promise written into it binds the operator, and this one was never decided by anyone. Its cost if wrong is asymmetric — deleting a clause now is one sentence, retracting a published guarantee later is not.

Fix: remove the "başka bir amaçla kullanmaz" guarantee from BOTH files. Keep the part the brief did ask for: the user owns what they write and upload, and grants the app permission to display it inside the app. Do not replace it with a broader licence grant either — do not swap one invented clause for another.

DO NOT change anything else in the document. If you notice other issues, list them in the fix report instead of changing them.

Then re-run:
    npm --prefix site run build
    node site/araclar/dogrula.mjs

`/kosullar` must still return 200, JS-disabled text length must stay above 400, no horizontal overflow at 1280/390. The tool still exits non-zero because /destek and /hesap-sil do not exist yet — that stays correct.

Stage only `docs/kullanim-kosullari.md` and `site/src/pages/kosullar.astro`. A parallel session is committing to this repo — never `git add -A`.

Append a fix report to `.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/task-5-report.md`: what you changed, the grep command and its output, the verification output. Then reply with the short status contract.

Bu, yapılmış işi etkilediği için şimdi netleştirmem gerekiyor — dört sayfa şu an tek dilli bir yapıda duruyor.

Yapıyı sonradan çok dilliye çevirmek, sayfaları `src/pages/gizlilik.astro`'dan `src/pages/[dil]/gizlilik.astro`'ya taşımak demek; şimdi karar verilirse bir kez yazılır, sonra verilirse dördü de yeniden düzenlenir. Yani asıl soru "yapı" değil, **çevirinin ne zaman ve hangi dillere** yapılacağı.

İki gerçeği söylemem gerekiyor:

Verify: read the content/ownership section in both files and quote what it now says. Check the two files still agree with each other.

The implementer was told to change ONLY these two things. If the fix diff touches anything else in the two in-scope files, that is new breakage — report it with severity and file:line.

Reply with, under 25 lines:

- **Finding 1:** ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED — with the grep output you ran, and confirmation the `.astro` file kept its accents.
- **Finding 2:** ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED — quote the wording now in each file, and state whether the two agree.
- **New breakage in the fix diff (in-scope files only):** none, or list each with severity and file:line.
- **Verdict:** all findings addressed / findings still open.

/gizlilik          -> Turkce (kok, DEGISMEZ)
/en/gizlilik       -> Ingilizce (dil acildiginda)

basvurularina ve gizlilik metnine yazilacak adresler kok adreslerdir,

yasandi (politika yazildi, tablo yetkisi verilmedi, ozellik aylarca olu
kaldi).

4. The button is re-enabled on every failure path (trace each `return`).
5. **Nothing is logged.** The error object, the password and the email must not reach `console.*`.
6. **Turkish accents** in the new strings (ç, ğ, ı, ö, ş, ü); code and comments ASCII; no circumflex letters (â, î).

The implementer was told explicitly to leave two other known Minor issues alone: the `invoke` error branch collapsing to "try later", and the comment numbering in `site/araclar/dogrula.mjs`. Those are deliberate. Do not flag them.

You are doing a SCOPED re-review of a one-finding fix. Verdict the finding ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED, and flag any new breakage introduced by the fix itself. Do not review anything outside this finding.

## Inputs

- **Fix diff (the only thing in scope):** `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/review-b5091ec..752a27d.diff`
- **Implementer's report (fix section at the end):** `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/task-7-report.md`

Repo root: `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud`. The only changed file is `site/src/betik/hesap-sil.ts` — read it to verify.

## Background

This is the account-deletion page of a public website for the Slooin mobile app. The user types email + password, the page signs in to get a JWT, then calls a Supabase Edge Function that re-verifies the password server-side and deletes the account. Google Play requires this page to exist.

## The finding that was sent for fixing

Every `signInWithPassword` failure produced the same message — "Giriş yapılamadı. E-posta ya da parola yanlış olabilir." — collapsing three different situations into one: a genuinely wrong password, a rate limit, and a network/server failure.

This matters because the same project already hit and fixed this exact bug on the server side (`mobil/supabase/functions/hesap-sil/index.ts`, comment block "DUZETME TURU 1"): telling someone their password is wrong when the server was merely unreachable makes them retry credentials and deepen a lockout.

**Required fix — three distinct branches:**

1. **Genuine credential failure** — detected as `code === 'invalid_credentials'`, or `status === 400` when `code` is absent (the same test the Edge Function uses). Keeps the original message, and **must still contain the sentence pointing people who never set a password to `destek@slooin.com`** — that is the only route for phone-registered accounts and for users who abandoned registration before setting a password.
2. **Rate limit** — `status === 429`. Must say the attempt was blocked by too many tries and to wait. **Must NOT say the password is wrong.**
3. **Everything else** — network failure, 5xx, unknown. Must say sign-in could not be completed right now, try again shortly or write to support. **Must NOT say the password is wrong.**

The button must be re-enabled in all three branches.

## Verify specifically

1. All three branches exist and their detection conditions match the spec above (check `429` and the `invalid_credentials` / `status === 400` pair).
2. Branch 2 and branch 3 messages contain no claim that the password or email is wrong. Read the actual Turkish strings.
3. Branch 1 still contains the `destek@slooin.com` fallback sentence. If that sentence was lost in the refactor, that is NOT ADDRESSED — it is the only path for a whole class of users.
4. The button is re-enabled on every failure path (trace each `return`).
5. **Nothing is logged.** The error object, the password and the email must not reach `console.*`.
6. **Turkish accents** in the new strings (ç, ğ, ı, ö, ş, ü); code and comments ASCII; no circumflex letters (â, î).

## Out of scope — do not report these

The implementer was told explicitly to leave two other known Minor issues alone: the `invoke` error branch collapsing to "try later", and the comment numbering in `site/araclar/dogrula.mjs`. Those are deliberate. Do not flag them.

Also out of scope: the Edge Function (must not be touched — confirm the diff does not touch it), and any account-status check (there must be none; suspended and frozen accounts stay deletable).

## Verification to run

    npm --prefix site run build
    node site/araclar/dogrula.mjs

It must exit 0 with all checks green. Report the exit code you observed.

## Report Format

Reply with, under 25 lines:

- **Finding:** ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED — quote each of the three branches' detection condition and its user-facing message.
- **Fallback sentence preserved:** yes/no, with the line.
- **Nothing logged:** yes/no.
- **New breakage in the fix diff:** none, or list each with severity and file:line.
- **Verification:** the exit code you observed.
- **Verdict:** finding addressed / still open.

## Task Description

Read your task brief first: `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/task-8-brief.md`

## Context

`site/` is a finished five-page Astro site for the Slooin mobile app — a public marketing + legal website. All five pages exist and `node site/araclar/dogrula.mjs` currently exits 0 with 25 green checks:

```
site/src/pages/index.astro      /
site/src/pages/gizlilik.astro   /gizlilik      (KVKK privacy policy)
site/src/pages/kosullar.astro   /kosullar      (terms of use)
site/src/pages/destek.astro     /destek        (support, Apple's Support URL)
site/src/pages/hesap-sil.astro  /hesap-sil     (account deletion, Play's requirement)
```

Shared pieces: `site/src/duzen/Duzen.astro` (props `baslik`, `aciklama`), `site/src/duzen/AltSerit.astro` (footer), `site/src/duzen/Metin.astro` (shell for the four text pages), `site/src/ortak/MarkaLockup.astro`, `site/src/ortak/Telefon.astro`.

Work from: `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud`
Branch: `claude/plan2-moderasyon-paneli`, already checked out — do not create a branch.

## The two invariants — everything else is negotiable, these are not

**1. The published URLs must not change.** `/gizlilik` stays `/gizlilik`. Turkish is the root language and takes no prefix; other languages would sit at `/en/gizlilik`. These exact addresses go into the App Store and Play Console submissions and into the privacy text itself — changing them later produces dead links in a store listing.

After your change, with `DILLER = ['tr']`, the built `site/dist/` must contain exactly the same page paths it contains right now. Compare before and after; if any path moved, you have broken the invariant.

**2. No empty language ships.** `DILLER` contains only `'tr'` in this release. A half-translated privacy policy is worse than an untranslated one: the missing or wrong sentence in a given language is the sentence that legally binds that user. In the app, a missing translation key falls back to Turkish (`mobil/src/lib/dil.tsx`); a legal document cannot fall back like that.

So: build the machinery, wire it up, prove it works — but publish only Turkish.

## Proving it works — this is the point of the task

Claiming "the structure is ready" without exercising it is exactly the failure this project has already lived through: migration `20260829090000` added an UPDATE policy for tag approval but never granted the table permission back, so the policy was dead code for months and nobody noticed, because nothing tested it.

So the verification tool must actually open a second language, build, measure, and restore. The brief describes this block. Key points:

- It temporarily rewrites `site/src/i18n/diller.ts` to add a second language, runs a build, measures, then **restores the file and rebuilds** — inside `try/finally`, so a mid-measurement error cannot leave `diller.ts` corrupted.
- It measures: all five pages generated under the second language; `hreflang` links present and **reciprocal** (the Turkish page points at both languages and so does the other one); `<html lang>` correct on the second language.
- After restoring, it asserts `site/dist/en/` does **not** exist — proving the shipped output really is Turkish-only.

**(a) `site/src/pages/destek.astro` heading levels.** The FAQ section title "Sık sorulan sorular" and each of the five questions are all `<h2>`, so the section title sits at the same outline level as its own contents and a screen-reader "jump by heading" pass cannot tell them apart. Make the five questions `<h3>` and add a matching `<h3>` rule to `Metin.astro`'s styles (follow the existing `<h2>` rule's approach). Do not change any wording.

**(b) `site/araclar/dogrula.mjs` section numbering.** The comment-numbered blocks no longer read in order top to bottom. After inserting your new block, renumber the comments so they read 1, 2, 3, … Cosmetic only — do not change any check's logic.

- **User-visible Turkish text carries accents** (ç, ğ, ı, ö, ş, ü). Code, identifiers, comments and commit messages stay ASCII. No circumflex letters (â, î).
- **Brand orange is exactly `#FE7813`.**
- No fabricated data.
- **No secrets in the repo** — it is public. `site/.env` is gitignored and must stay untracked.

## Environment facts, already measured — do not re-derive

- **Do NOT pass Turkish accented characters through a bash heredoc on this machine** — they get mangled. Use the Write tool for any file with Turkish text.
- Use FORWARD slashes in script paths on Windows.

## Committing

**A parallel session is committing to this same repo right now** (`CLAUDE.md`, `mobil/*`, `docs/oturumlar/*`, `tasarim/*.png` change under you).

**Never use `git add -A`, `git add .`, or `git commit -a`.** Stage only your own paths under `site/`. Run `git status --short` before committing and confirm nothing outside `site/` is staged, and that `site/.env` is not staged.

## Your Job

Follow the brief's steps in order — it is test-first: the verification block goes in first and must FAIL before `diller.ts` exists.

Finish with:

```bash
npm --prefix site run build
node site/araclar/dogrula.mjs
```

**This must exit 0.** Anything still failing is a real problem — diagnose it, never weaken a check to get green.

**While you work:** if something unexpected comes up — Astro's routing not producing an unprefixed root language, `getStaticPaths` fighting the layout, the temporary-rebuild block being slow or flaky — **ask**. Don't guess, and don't quietly change the URL scheme to make routing easier.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do all of this yourself. Never spawn a subagent, and never spawn a reviewer — review is the controller's job and is already scheduled after your report.

## When You're in Over Your Head

It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard." Bad work is worse than no work. Report BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT with what you tried and what help you need.

## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review

Check with commands, not by eye — a previous task claimed a visual check and was wrong:
- List the built page paths before and after your change and confirm they are identical.
- Confirm `site/dist/en/` does not exist after a normal build.
- Confirm `git status --short` shows `site/src/i18n/diller.ts` restored to `['tr']` (the tool rewrites it temporarily).
- Confirm the accents survived: `grep -c "ğ\|ş\|ç\|ö\|ü\|ı" site/dist/gizlilik/index.html`.

## After Review Findings

If the task review finds issues, you will be resumed with them. Fix them, re-run the verification tool, and append a fix report to the same report file: what changed, the command run, and its output. Then reply with the same short status contract.

## Report Format

Write your full report to:
`C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/task-8-report.md`

Include: what you implemented; RED/GREEN evidence for the new multilingual checks; **the before/after list of built page paths proving URLs did not change**; the full verification output with its exit code; how you handled the two small debts; files changed; self-review findings; concerns.

Then reply with ONLY (under 15 lines):
- **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
- Commit created (short SHA + subject)
- One-line test summary
- Concerns, if any

## Inputs — read all three

1. **Task brief (the requirements):** `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/task-8-brief.md`
   NOTE: this file was stale while the implementer worked (a controller bookkeeping error — briefs were extracted before the plan was renumbered). It has since been regenerated and is now correct. 3. **Review package:** `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/review-c24aad1..c9534f9.diff`

Repo root: `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud`.

## What this task is

`site/` is a five-page Astro website for the Slooin mobile app: a homepage plus four pages that App Store and Google Play reviewers read — `/gizlilik` (KVKK privacy policy), `/kosullar` (terms), `/destek` (Apple's required Support URL), `/hesap-sil` (Play's required web account-deletion page).

This task makes the site multilingual **in structure only**. Turkish is the root language and takes no URL prefix; other languages would sit under `/en/...`. Only Turkish ships.

## The two invariants — check these first and hardest

**1. Published URLs must not have changed.** `/gizlilik` must still be `/gizlilik`. These addresses go into store submissions and into the privacy text itself; a moved URL becomes a dead link in a store listing.

I verified the built output myself after the commit — `site/dist` contains exactly `/index.html`, `/gizlilik/`, `/kosullar/`, `/destek/`, `/hesap-sil/` and no `/en/`. **Do not re-derive that; instead check whether anything in the code could break it later** — e.g. a `getStaticPaths` that would emit a `/tr/` prefix if the language list grew, or a hard-coded path that assumes the root language.

**2. No empty language ships.** `DILLER` must contain only `'tr'`. A half-translated privacy policy is worse than an untranslated one — the missing sentence in a language is the sentence that binds that user. Confirm nothing publishes a second language today.

## The point of this task: the "structure is ready" claim must be tested

This project has already shipped a dead feature because nothing exercised it: migration `20260829090000` added an UPDATE policy for tag approval but never granted the table permission back, so the policy was dead code for months.

So the verification tool is supposed to temporarily add a second language, rebuild, measure, then restore and rebuild.

**Review that block as a test, sceptically:**

- Does it genuinely rebuild with a second language, or does it assert against something that would pass anyway?
- Would it FAIL if `hreflang` links were one-directional instead of reciprocal? If `<html lang>` were wrong? If a page were missing under the second language?
- Is the restore inside `try/finally`, so a mid-measurement failure cannot leave `site/src/i18n/diller.ts` corrupted with a language that then ships?
- **After a normal build, does it actually assert `/en/` is absent** — or only that it exists during the temporary build?
- Check `git status --short` and confirm `diller.ts` is not left modified in the working tree.

## Also verify

3. **The `[...dil]` rest-parameter choice.** The implementer reports that Astro 7.3.1 rejects the non-spread optional segment `[[dil]]` with "Missing parameter: dil", so a rest parameter was used instead. That is a reasonable deviation if true. Sanity-check the `getStaticPaths` implementations: with one language, do they emit exactly one route each with an empty prefix?
4. **Two small debts folded into this task:**
   - `destek.astro`: the five FAQ questions should now be `<h3>` under the `<h2>` section title, with a matching `<h3>` rule added to `Metin.astro`. Wording must be unchanged.
   - `site/araclar/dogrula.mjs`: section comment numbers should read 1, 2, 3 … top to bottom. Cosmetic only — verify no check's logic changed.
5. **`hreflang` correctness.** Read how the alternate links are built. Do they produce correct absolute URLs for both the root language (no prefix) and a prefixed one? A naive string concat often yields `//gizlilik` or `/en//gizlilik`.
6. **The language switcher** must not render at all when only one language is enabled — a one-option switcher offers the user nothing.
7. **No secrets.** `site/.env` must remain untracked and unstaged.
8. **Nothing outside `site/` was committed.** A parallel session is working in this repo on `CLAUDE.md`, `mobil/*`, `docs/oturumlar/*`, `tasarim/*.png`. Check with `git show --stat c9534f9`.

## Global Constraints

- User-visible Turkish text carries accents (ç, ğ, ı, ö, ş, ü). Code, identifiers, comments and commit messages stay ASCII. No circumflex letters (â, î).
- Brand orange is exactly `#FE7813`.
- No fabricated data.

## Expected outcome

`node site/araclar/dogrula.mjs` must exit 0. If it does not, that is a real finding — never accept a weakened check as the reason it passes.

## Review method

Read the diff and the files. Run cheap read-only checks that settle a question (`npm --prefix site run build`, `node site/araclar/dogrula.mjs`, listing built paths, greps). The multilingual block rebuilds twice, so the tool is slower than before — that is expected, not a defect, unless it is so slow as to be unusable.

Judge severity honestly: **Critical** (a URL moved, a second language ships, a secret leaks), **Important** (a check that cannot fail, malformed hreflang, `diller.ts` left dirty, a debt not actually fixed), **Minor** (naming, markup polish). Do not inflate or suppress. If you suspect a false positive, report it and say why you are unsure — the controller adjudicates.

## Report Format

**Spec compliance: ✅ or ❌**
- If ❌, each missing/incorrect requirement with the brief's wording and what the code does instead.
- Anything implemented that the brief did NOT ask for.

**Task quality: Approved or Changes requested**
- Strengths (brief).
- Findings: severity, file:line, what is wrong, why it matters.
- **Test scepticism:** your explicit answer on whether the multilingual checks could fail, and what would make each one fail.
- `⚠️ Cannot verify from diff:` anything you could not check, and why.

Keep it under 60 lines. Be specific with file:line references.

    EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
    SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY

3. Assert the page shows the success message and hides the form.
4. **Assert a fresh `signInWithPassword` with those same credentials now fails.** This is the assertion that matters — the rest is UI theatre without it.

If step 4 passes while the account still exists, the test is worthless. Make sure it queries the real auth endpoint, not a cached client.

- User-visible Turkish text carries accents (ç, ğ, ı, ö, ş, ü). Code, identifiers, comments and commit messages stay ASCII. No circumflex letters (â, î).
- No fabricated data.
- **No secrets in the repo.** It is public.

- `puppeteer-core` lives at `mobil/node_modules/puppeteer-core`; its ESM entry is `lib/puppeteer/puppeteer-core.js` (NOT `lib/esm/...`).

- `site/.env` exists locally (gitignored) with the two `PUBLIC_*` values; the site build already uses it.

## Committing

**A parallel session is committing to this repo** (`CLAUDE.md`, `mobil/*`, `docs/oturumlar/*`, `tasarim/*.png`).

**Never `git add -A`, `git add .`, or `git commit -a`.** Stage exactly:

    git add araclar/site-silme-test-hesabi.py site/araclar/silme-canli-test.mjs

Run `git status --short` first; confirm nothing else is staged and `site/.env` is not among them.

## Your Job

Write both scripts, then actually run the end-to-end test and report its real output. A test that was written but never run does not close this gap.

Also confirm `node site/araclar/dogrula.mjs` still exits 0 afterwards.

**While you work:** if something is unclear or the live run behaves unexpectedly, **ask**. Do not guess against a production system.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do all of this yourself. Never spawn a subagent, and never spawn a reviewer — review is the controller's job and is already scheduled.

It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard." Bad work is worse than no work. Report BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT with what you tried — especially if account creation is refused, the form will not submit headless, or the deletion returns an error you do not understand. **Do not start improvising against the live project.**

## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review

Check: does the test assert the account is really gone, not just that the UI looked right; is any key printed anywhere; did you touch only the account you created; is `site/.env` unstaged; does `dogrula.mjs` still exit 0.

Write your full report to:
`C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/task-9-report.md`

Include: both corrections you applied and why; the real end-to-end run output with each assertion's result; explicit confirmation that the throwaway account no longer exists (or, if it does, its exact address); `git status --short` proving what was staged; concerns.

**Never put a real key or project URL in the report.**

Then reply with ONLY (under 15 lines):
- **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
- Commit created (short SHA + subject)
- One-line test summary
- Concerns, if any
- The report file path

**Canlı test gerçek bir üretim hatası buldu: hesap silme şu anda çalışmıyor.**

Depodaki kod doğru — 1-2 Eylül'de kimliği e-postaya taşırken fonksiyonu da güncellemişiz (önce e-posta, sonra telefon). Ama **o değişiklik hiç dağıtılmamış.** Canlıdaki sürüm 5 ve ~21 Ağustos'tan kalma; e-posta yolunu hiç tanımıyor, JWT'de telefon bulamayınca "Bu hesap parola ile doğrulanamıyor" deyip reddediyor.

CLAUDE.md bunu zaten kayda geçmiş: "Supabase auth admin silme bu projede sık sık zaman aşımına düşüyor." Yani yeniden dağıtım gerekli ama yeterli olmayabilir; o ayrı bir teşhis işi.

content.text: Dağıtım birinci hatayı çözdü ama **hesap silme hâlâ çalışmıyor**: `auth.admin.deleteUser` 504'lerle zaman aşımına düşüyor. Bu, Play'in zorunlu tuttuğu bir işlev, yani "bilinen tuhaflık" deyip geçemem. Somut bir hipotezim var ve ölçülebilir: `auth.users` silinirken tetiklenen cascade'de **indekssiz bir yabancı anahtar** varsa, silme sıralı tarama yapar ve büyük tablolarda zaman aşımına düşer.

input.query:
-- auth.users'a bakan yabanci anahtarlar ve o sutunda indeks var mi
select
  c.conrelid::regclass::text            as tablo,
  a.attname                             as sutun,
  c.confdeltype                          as silme_kurali,
  exists (
    select 1 from pg_index i
    where i.indrelid = c.conrelid
      and a.attnum = any(i.indkey)
      and i.indkey[0] = a.attnum
  )                                      as indeksli,
  pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(c.conrelid)) as boyut
from pg_constraint c
join unnest(c.conkey) with ordinality as k(attnum, ord) on true
join pg_attribute a on a.attrelid = c.conrelid and a.attnum = k.attnum
where c.contype = 'f'
  and c.confrelid = 'auth.users'::regclass
order by indeksli, pg_total_relation_size(c.conrelid) desc;

**Kök nedeni buldum ve "bilinen tuhaflık" değil.** Listenin ilk satırı:

```
mekanlar.ekleyen_kullanici -> auth.users   ON DELETE SET NULL   INDEKSLI: false   4450 MB
```

Bir kullanıcı silinirken Postgres, `mekanlar` içinde o kullanıcıya ait satırları bulup `NULL`'a çekmek zorunda. O sütunda indeks yok — yani **her hesap silme işlemi 4,45 GB'lık, 5,9 milyon satırlık tabloyu baştan sona tarıyor.** 10 saniyelik zaman aşımının sebebi bu. Diğer indekssiz yabancı anahtarların tabloları 96 kB ve altında, onlar önemsiz.

content.text:
Ölçüm hipotezi doğruladı: planlayıcı **`Parallel Seq Scan on mekanlar`** seçiyor, tahmini maliyet 279.186. Her hesap silme işlemi bunu yapıyor.

Yani bu, Supabase'in kararsızlığı değil, bizim şemamızdaki eksik bir indeks. CLAUDE.md bunu "sık sık zaman aşımına düşüyor" diye kaydetmiş ama teşhis edilmemiş — silme bu yüzden aylardır kırık.

Düzeltmesi tek satır ve toplama yönünde (veri değiştirmiyor):

```sql
create index concurrently mekanlar_ekleyen_kullanici_idx
  on public.mekanlar (ekleyen_kullanici)
  where ekleyen_kullanici is not null;
```

Kısmi indeks seçiyorum çünkü `mekanlar`daki 5,98 milyon kaydın neredeyse tamamı Foursquare'den geliyor ve `ekleyen_kullanici` alanı boş; yalnızca kullanıcının kendi eklediği mekanlar dolu. Yani indeks kilobayt mertebesinde kalır, tam indeks ise ~130 MB olurdu.

-- NEDEN KISMI INDEKS: `mekanlar` kayitlarinin neredeyse tamami
-- Foursquare'den geliyor ve `ekleyen_kullanici` alanlari NULL; yalnizca

create index if not exists mekanlar_ekleyen_kullanici_idx

  where ekleyen_kullanici is not null;

input.message:
Root cause of the 504 is found and fixed — re-run your end-to-end test one more time.

You were right that the redeploy was necessary but not sufficient, and right not to paper over the timeout. I diagnosed it: `mekanlar.ekleyen_kullanici` is a foreign key to `auth.users` with ON DELETE SET NULL, and **it had no index**. So every account deletion made Postgres scan the whole `mekanlar` table — 5.98 million rows, 4450 MB — to find rows to null out. That is what was blowing the 10-second timeout, on every attempt, for any account.

Measured, before and after:

    before: Parallel Seq Scan on mekanlar, cost 279186
    after : Index Scan using mekanlar_ekleyen_kullanici_idx
            Buffers: shared hit=1, Execution Time 0.850 ms

The second EXPLAIN used `FOR KEY SHARE`, the exact query shape the FK trigger issues, so this is the real path and not an approximation. The index is a partial one (`where ekleyen_kullanici is not null`), 16 kB, valid and ready. It was created with CONCURRENTLY on production with the user's approval, and I have written the matching migration file into the repo.

WHAT TO DO NOW

Re-run the full end-to-end test: fresh throwaway account, delete it through the built `/hesap-sil` page in a real browser, and assert all three — success message shown, form hidden, and a fresh `signInWithPassword` with those credentials now rejected.

Report the real timings. I want to see how long `deleteUser` takes now; if it is fast, say how fast.

IF IT STILL FAILS
Report it plainly with the status codes and durations. Do not add retries, do not loop for a green result, do not weaken an assertion. A third distinct cause would itself be worth knowing.

CLEANUP AND LIMITS — unchanged
- There are now 4 leftover throwaway accounts from earlier runs. Do not delete them and do not write a sweeper. At the end, list every `silme-testi-*@slooin.test` address that still exists so they can be cleared manually.
- Only ever touch the account this run creates.
- Never print a service-role key, anon key, or the project URL.
- Do not modify the Edge Function, the migration, or any other repo file.
- Confirm `node site/araclar/dogrula.mjs` still exits 0.

Append a new section to `.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/task-9-report.md` for this run, then reply with the short status contract.

`site/src/pages/[...dil]/gizlilik.astro:149-151` "bu denetim izi bugün henüz kurulmadı… moderasyon paneliyle birlikte gelecek" ve `:212-218` "Planlanan (henüz uygulanmadı): moderasyon erişim kayıtlarının 2 yıl… o tablo henüz veritabanında yok". Canlıda ölçtüm: `moderasyon_kayitlari` **var** ve `moderasyon-izi-buda` cron'u `interval '2 years'` ile her gün çalışıyor. Yani metin, gerçekte var olan bir korumayı ve yürürlükteki bir saklama süresini "yok" diye ilan ediyor. Kaynak metinde de aynı: `docs/gizlilik-metni.md:136,181-183`, `mobil/src/app/gizlilik.tsx:63,82`. Ruling R8'in kendi gerekçesi ("bu metni ilk kez herkese açık yayınlıyoruz") aynen buraya da uyar.

Kimlik 2026-09-01/02'de e-postaya taşındı (`mobil/src/app/(auth)/kayit.tsx:79` `signInWithOtp({ email })`), ve bu planın kendi silme formu `hesap-sil.astro:58` **e-posta** istiyor. Apple'ın App Privacy beyanında "Email Address" işaretlenecek; politika ile beyan uyuşmazlığı doğrudan inceleme riski.

Kullanıcı uygulamada bir şey, sitede başka bir şey okuyor. Bu, Task 4'te sitede düzeltilen çelişkinin (Ruling R8 #1) uygulama tarafındaki eşi.

You are applying the fix wave from a final review. Seven findings, listed below. Fix all of them, then verify and commit once.

Repo root: `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud`. Branch `claude/plan2-moderasyon-paneli`, already checked out — do not create a branch.

## Context

A public website for the Slooin mobile app was just built at `site/` (Astro, static). Five pages: `/` and four that Apple and Google Play reviewers read — `/gizlilik` (KVKK privacy policy), `/kosullar` (terms), `/destek` (Apple's Support URL), `/hesap-sil` (Play's required web account-deletion page).

The privacy text exists in **three** places that must agree:
- `docs/gizlilik-metni.md` — the source document
- `site/src/pages/[...dil]/gizlilik.astro` — the published website page
- `mobil/src/app/gizlilik.tsx` — the in-app screen (text is copied into code deliberately, so it reads offline)

Website pages carry **accented Turkish** (ç, ğ, ı, ö, ş, ü). `docs/gizlilik-metni.md` is **ASCII from line 14 onward** — match each file's existing convention. No circumflex letters (â, î). Code, identifiers, comments and commit messages stay ASCII.

`site/araclar/dogrula.mjs` is the verification tool; `npm --prefix site run build && node site/araclar/dogrula.mjs` must exit 0 when you are done.

---

## FINDING 1 (Critical) — the privacy text denies protections that actually exist

`site/src/pages/[...dil]/gizlilik.astro` around lines 149-151 and 212-218 says the moderation audit trail "bugün henüz kurulmadı", will arrive "moderasyon paneliyle birlikte", and that a 2-year retention for moderation access records is "Planlanan (henüz uygulanmadı)… o tablo henüz veritabanında yok".

**All of that is false.** I measured it on the live database just now:

    moderasyon_kayitlari tablosu    : VAR (0 satir, ama tablo mevcut)
    cron isi                        : moderasyon-izi-buda, her gun 04:45
    budama araligi                  : 2 yil

So the document tells users a safeguard does not exist when it does, and calls a live retention rule "planned". A legal document that understates its own protections is still a false statement, and this one is about to be handed to store reviewers.

Fix: rewrite those passages to describe what is actually in place — moderator access to private messages is recorded in an append-only audit table, and those records are pruned after two years by a daily job. Keep the tone of the surrounding text. Do not overstate either: the table currently holds zero rows because no moderator access has happened yet, and if you want to say that, say it plainly.

Apply the same correction in `docs/gizlilik-metni.md` (ASCII) and `mobil/src/app/gizlilik.tsx`.

## FINDING 2 (Critical) — email is missing from the processed-data list

`gizlilik.astro:29` lists "Telefon numaran (hesap ve doğrulama için)" and `:50` talks about verifying the phone number. Authentication moved from phone to **email** on 2026-09-01/02 (`mobil/src/app/(auth)/kayit.tsx` uses `signInWithOtp({ email })`), and this site's own deletion form asks for an email.

Measured on the live database: **10 of 13 accounts have an email; 3 do not** (older phone-registered accounts that still work).

So the privacy policy fails to disclose the primary identifier we collect today. Apple's App Privacy declaration will list "Email Address"; a policy that does not mention it is a direct review risk.

Fix: add the email address to the processed-data list and to the verification description, as the primary account identifier. Keep phone number listed too — those older accounts exist and phone login still works — but describe it accurately as the legacy identifier rather than the current one. Same in all three files.

## FINDING 3 (Important) — KVKK requires the legal basis, and none is stated

`gizlilik.astro` section 2 lists only purposes. Neither "sözleşmenin ifası" nor "açık rıza" nor "meşru menfaat" appears anywhere (grep returns zero). KVKK m.10 requires the legal basis for processing, and m.9 requires a basis for transfers abroad; section 5 describes transfers without naming one.

Fix: state the legal basis for each processing purpose. Ground each one — do not invent:
- Account data (email, name, username, date of birth) and location/check-in: **sözleşmenin ifası** — the app literally cannot function without a check-in; this reasoning is already recorded in the project (see `CLAUDE.md`, the note that location's basis is contract performance and the app does not work without check-in).
- Moderation and security records: **meşru menfaat** (abuse and harassment prevention).
- Anything the app takes explicit consent for is recorded in the `kvkk_onaylari` table — check what is actually stored there before describing it.

For transfers abroad (section 5), state the basis honestly. If you cannot ground a claim about the transfer mechanism, **write what is true and flag the remainder in your report instead of inventing a mechanism**.

Also update `docs/kvkk-uyum-listesi.md` — it already records this gap; mark it closed with what you wrote. That file is the project's living KVKK checklist and the project's own rule is that it gets updated whenever a work item touches personal data.

## FINDING 4 (Important) — the in-app screen contradicts the website

`docs/gizlilik-metni.md` gained a "Veri sorumlusu" section and the real support address (`destek@slooin.com`, answered within 30 days), but `mobil/src/app/gizlilik.tsx:93` still says "bugün için somut bir destek kanalı yayında değil — bu bir yer tutucudur" and the screen has no data-controller section.

The file's own stated rule is that the on-screen text is copied from the source document. Right now a user reads one thing in the app and another on the website.

Fix: bring `mobil/src/app/gizlilik.tsx` in line — add the data-controller section (veri sorumlusu: **Orçun Özdemir**, contact `destek@slooin.com`, applications answered within 30 days at the latest; **the postal address is NOT published** — that was the user's explicit decision) and replace the placeholder text with the real channel. This screen is user-facing: accented Turkish.

## FINDING 5 (Important) — the duplication is undocumented

`site/README.md` never mentions that `docs/gizlilik-metni.md` / `docs/kullanim-kosullari.md` and their Astro pages are the same text in two (for privacy, three) places, or who is responsible for keeping them in sync. Finding 4 is exactly what that gap produces.

Fix: add a short, prominent section to `site/README.md` naming all three locations of the privacy text and both locations of the terms, and stating that a change to one must be applied to all.

## FINDING 6 (Minor) — the verification tool only runs on one machine

`site/araclar/dogrula.mjs` hard-codes an absolute puppeteer path and Chrome path under `C:/Users/orcns/...`. On any other machine — or CI — the site's only test harness cannot run.

Fix: keep the current values as the fallback, but let both be overridden by environment variables, and fail with a clear message naming the variable if the executable is not found. Do not restructure the tool.

## FINDING 7 (Minor) — the favicon is invisible on a light browser tab

`site/src/duzen/Duzen.astro:26` points the favicon at `/marka-isareti.png`, whose opaque pixels average (255,255,255) — a white mark on a white tab.

Fix: copy `mobil/assets/images/marka-isareti-acik.png` (the orange variant, average (249,93,2)) into `site/public/` under a distinct name and point the favicon at it. **Do not change** the existing `/marka-isareti.png` — the page uses it deliberately on the orange hero, where white is correct.

- Do not change `site/src/pages/[...dil]/kosullar.astro` or `docs/kullanim-kosullari.md` except where Finding 3 or 5 genuinely requires it. The review confirmed those two are already consistent with each other.
- Do not add retry logic anywhere, do not weaken any check in `dogrula.mjs`, and do not create stub pages.

- **Do NOT pass Turkish accented characters through a bash heredoc on this machine** — they get mangled. Use the Write/Edit tools for files with Turkish text.

**A parallel session is committing to this repo** (`CLAUDE.md`, `mobil/app.json`, `docs/oturumlar/*`, `tasarim/*.png`). **Never `git add -A`, `git add .`, or `git commit -a`.** Stage only the files you actually changed, by path. Run `git status --short` first and confirm nothing else is staged.

You are doing the single SCOPED re-review of a seven-finding fix wave. Verdict each finding ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED, and flag any new breakage the fix itself introduced. Do not review anything outside these findings.

## Inputs

- **Fix diff (one commit, the whole wave):** `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/review-698bbfb..460f1fe.diff`
- **Report (two agents appended to it — the first was killed mid-run by a rate limit, the second finished):** `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-slooin-web-sitesi/final-fix-report.md`

Repo root: `C:/Users/orcns/projects/cloud`. Read any file to verify.

## Background

A public website for the Slooin mobile app (`site/`, Astro, static). Apple and Google Play reviewers read four of its five pages. The privacy text lives in **three** places that must agree:

- `docs/gizlilik-metni.md` — source document, **ASCII** from the body onward
- `site/src/pages/[...dil]/gizlilik.astro` — website page, **accented Turkish**
- `mobil/src/app/gizlilik.tsx` — in-app screen, **accented Turkish** (text copied into code so it reads offline)

## The seven findings

**1 (Critical) — the privacy text denied a safeguard that exists.** It said the moderation audit trail "henüz kurulmadı" and that the 2-year retention was "planlanan (henüz uygulanmadı)". I measured the live database: `moderasyon_kayitlari` exists and the cron job `moderasyon-izi-buda` runs daily at 04:45 pruning at 2 years. The text had to be corrected in all three files.

Verify the corrected passages are accurate and do not now **overstate** either — the table genuinely holds zero rows today because no moderator access has happened.

Careful: the phrase "henüz uygulanmadı" still appears in these files about a **different** subject — the planned 1-year deletion of resolved complaints, which really is not implemented. Those statements are TRUE. Do not flag them.

**2 (Critical) — email was missing from the processed-data list.** Authentication moved from phone to email on 2026-09-01/02; 10 of 13 live accounts have an email. The policy listed only the phone number. Email had to be added as the primary identifier, with phone kept and described as the legacy one.

**3 (Important) — no legal basis was stated.** KVKK m.10 requires it. The fix should state sözleşmenin ifası for account data and location/check-in, meşru menfaat for moderation and security records, and describe consent accurately against what `kvkk_onaylari` actually stores. **Check these are grounded, not decorative.** If the transfer-abroad section (m.9) now asserts a mechanism, judge whether it is supportable; the fixer was told to leave it unwritten and flag it rather than invent one. Read the report's "could not ground" list.

**4 (Important) — the in-app screen contradicted the website.** `mobil/src/app/gizlilik.tsx` still said "bugün için somut bir destek kanalı yayında değil — bu bir yer tutucudur" and had no data-controller section, while the source document and website had both. Verify it now matches, including: veri sorumlusu **Orçun Özdemir**, contact `destek@slooin.com`, applications answered within 30 days, and **no postal address** (its absence was a deliberate decision — if an address appeared, that is a finding).

**5 (Important) — the duplication was undocumented.** `site/README.md` had to gain a section naming all three privacy locations and both terms locations, and stating that a change to one must be applied to all in the same commit.

**6 (Minor) — the verification tool only ran on one machine.** `site/araclar/dogrula.mjs` hard-coded absolute puppeteer and Chrome paths. Both had to become environment-overridable (`SLOOIN_PUPPETEER`, `SLOOIN_CHROME`) with the old values as fallbacks and a clear failure message naming the variable. **Verify no check's logic changed** — this file is the site's only test harness.

**7 (Minor) — the favicon was invisible on a light tab.** It pointed at a white mark. A distinct orange asset had to be added and the favicon repointed. **`site/public/marka-isareti.png` must still exist unchanged** — the hero uses it on the orange background where white is correct.

## Verify these yourself

- Run `npm --prefix site run build` then `node site/araclar/dogrula.mjs`. It must exit 0.
- Run `cd mobil && npx jest __tests__/ekranlar/gizlilik.test.tsx` — the wave changed that test. It must pass, and the changed assertions must actually assert the new content rather than having been loosened to accommodate it. **Read the test diff with that suspicion.**
- Confirm the three privacy texts agree on: the data controller, `destek@slooin.com`, and the audit-trail-is-in-force statement.

  **A warning about your tooling:** `grep -i` is unreliable for Turkish accented characters in this environment — I got a false mismatch on "yürürlüktedir" versus "YURURLUKTEDIR" because the case folding failed on `ü`/`Ü`. Compare with case-sensitive greps for each spelling, or read the passages, rather than trusting one `-i` search.

- Confirm the ASCII/accent conventions held: `docs/gizlilik-metni.md` body ASCII (`grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7F]'`), the two screens accented.

## Out of scope — do not report

- The parallel session's files (`CLAUDE.md`, `mobil/app.json`, `docs/oturumlar/*`, `tasarim/*.png`). Confirm none were swept into this commit, then ignore them.
- The remaining known deferred items: the live-deletion test's regex not matching two of five error strings (fails loudly, no false-green risk), and the `invoke` error branch collapsing to one message (that branch is unreachable because the password was already validated at sign-in).

## Do not

- Do not run the live deletion test (`silme-canli-test.mjs`) — it creates and deletes a real account.
- Do not modify any file. This is a review.
- Do not delete, query or modify any user account.

## Report Format

Reply with, under 40 lines:

- **Each finding 1-7:** ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED, with file:line and the actual text now there for 1-4.
- **Legal accuracy check:** does anything in the privacy text now claim something the app does not do, or overstate a safeguard? Quote it.
- **Test integrity:** were the jest assertions strengthened to match new content, or loosened to let it pass?
- **New breakage in the fix diff:** none, or each with severity and file:line.
- **Verdict:** all findings addressed / findings still open.

content.text:
İş bitti ve push edildi. Çalışma alanını sildim; kayıt artık git geçmişinde.

## Ne yapıldı

**15 commit, 10 görev**, her biri ayrı bir incelemeden geçti, sonunda bütün plan için bir final incelemesi ve tek bir düzeltme turu. `slooin.com` için beş sayfa: ana sayfa, gizlilik politikası, kullanım koşulları, destek ve hesap silme. Doğrulama aracı 36 kontrolle sıfır çıkış veriyor.

**Ama bu işin asıl getirisi site değil.** Hesap silme sayfası için yazdığımız canlı uçtan uca test, **iki gerçek üretim hatası** buldu — ikisi de yalnızca sitede değil, uygulamanın kendisinde de kırıktı:

1. **`hesap-sil` fonksiyonu 21 Ağustos'tan kalmaydı.** Kimliği e-postaya taşırken kodu güncellemişiz ama hiç dağıtmamışız. Sonuç: 1 Eylül'den beri açılmış her hesap — hepsi e-postalı — hesabını silemiyordu. Senin onayınla sürüm 6 dağıtıldı.
2. **`mekanlar.ekleyen_kullanici` indekssizdi.** `auth.users`'a bakan bir yabancı anahtar, ve her hesap silme işlemi 4,45 GB'lık tabloyu baştan sona tarıyordu. CLAUDE.md bunu "sık sık zaman aşımına düşüyor" diye kaydetmiş ama teşhis edilmemişti. `deleteUser` 10+ saniyelik zaman aşımından **58,7 milisaniyeye** indi.

Final inceleme de gizlilik metninde iki ciddi hata buldu: metin **gerçekte yürürlükte olan** bir denetim izini "henüz kurulmadı" diye ilan ediyordu, ve bugün topladığımız birincil kimlik verisini — e-postayı — hiç saymıyordu.

## Senin adına verdiğim kararlar

Bunları sen sormadan verdim; yanlış bulduğunu geri aldırabilirsin.

| Karar | Yanlışsa maliyeti |
|---|---|
| **R1** Ayrı worktree açmadım (doğrulama araçları `mobil/node_modules`'a bağımlı) | Site commit'leri bu dalın geçmişine karıştı; ayırmak cherry-pick gerektirir |
| **R2** Test betiğindeki `SUPABASE_URL` → `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | Betik ilk koşumda hata verirdi, ucuz |
| **R3** Ekran görüntüsü aracını Task 3 kapsamına aldım, sonra ölçüp daralttım | Araç değişikliği diğer görüntü işlerini etkiler; eski değişken adı korundu |
| **R4** `dogrula.mjs` bölüm numaralarını okuma sırasına göre yeniden verdirdim | Yok, kozmetik |
| **R5** Test kabuğuna eksik `PUBLIC_*` export'larını ekletttim | Eksik kalsa test son kontrolde patlardı |
| **R6** Adını tahmin etmedim, yer tutucu bıraktım | Sen adını verene kadar yayın bloke olurdu |
| **R7** Ekran görüntülerini şimdi yeniden çektirmedim | Ana sayfa geçici olarak eski ekranları gösteriyor; site yayında değil |
| **R8** Gizlilik metnindeki iki çelişkiyi düzelttirdim (biri önceden vardı) | Hukuki metinde bir cümle fazladan değişmiş olur, git'te görünür |
| **R9** `.md` ASCII, sayfa aksanlı — dosyaların kendi kuralına uydurdum | Toplu aksan dönüşümü riski alınmadı (2026-08-23'te kod bozmuştu) |
| **R10** "Uygulama içeriği başka amaçla kullanmaz" taahhüdünü Minor'dan yükseltip sildirdim | O taahhüdü istiyorsan tek cümleyle geri konur |
| **R11** Giriş hatasını üç dala ayırttım (Minor'dan yükselttim) | Üç dallı mesaj bloğu tek dala indirilebilir |
| **R12** `invoke` hatalarının tek mesaja toplanmasını park ettim (o dal erişilemez) | Yok |
| **R13** Numaralandırma düzeltmesini Task 8'e iliştirdim | Yok |
| **—** `finishing-a-development-branch` becerisini çağırmadım | Entegrasyon yolu CLAUDE.md'de zaten yazılı: commit + push. Ayrı bir özellik dalı yok |

Bir de kendi hatam: brief dosyalarını plana yeni görev eklemeden önce çıkarmıştım, yeniden numaralandırma onları sessizce bayatlattı. Alt ajan fark edip plandan çalıştı; brief'leri yeniden ürettim.

## Sende kalanlar

**Mağaza başvurusundan önce:**
- `slooin.com` satın alınması, Cloudflare Pages projesi ve **`destek@slooin.com` kutusunun gerçekten açılması** — şu an üç sayfa da var olmayan bir adrese "üç iş günü içinde yanıtlanır" diyor
- Ekran görüntülerinin yeniden çekilmesi (sen ekran değişikliklerini bitirince, tercihen telefon derlemesinden — web sürümünde gerçek harita yok)
- Saklama süresi kararı: check-in görünürlük süresi kullanıcının seçeceği bir ayara dönüşünce gizlilik metnindeki ifadeler somut süreyle güncellenmeli

**Dört atılabilir test hesabı duruyor**, silmedim (`silme-testi-6648500c`, `f58ed6e1`, `d66fbd13` @slooin.test ve `+905559938018`). Silme artık çalışıyor; temizlememi istersen söyle.

Kısayol hazır: **`Masaüstü\Claude - vpn.bat`**

Ama önce bir şeyi söylemem gerekiyor, çünkü senin tarifinle diskteki durum uyuşmuyor:

**`vpn` diye bir klasör hiçbir yerde yoktu.** Masaüstünde, `projects/` altında ve ev dizininde dört seviye derinlikte arattım — yok. `yeni-uygulama` da bir Flutter projesi, o değil. Kısayolun boş bir yola bakması işe yaramayacağı için klasörü ben oluşturdum: `C:\Users\orcns\projects\vpn`.

Diğer üç projenin hepsi `projects/` altında ve masaüstünde yalnızca `.bat` kısayolları duruyor; aynı düzeni izledim. Projeyi gerçekten masaüstünün *içine* koymak istiyorsan ya da başka bir yerde başlattıysan, tek satır söyle — kısayolu oraya çeviririm.

**Klasörü `git init` ile açtım ve bu isteğe bağlı bir tercih değil.** Mevcut `Claude - yeni uygulama.bat` dosyasının içinde yaşanmış bir olayın kaydı duruyordu; teyit ettim: oturum kaydı hook'u `~/.claude/settings.json` içinde **global** kayıtlı, yani hangi klasörden açarsan aç çalışıyor ve depo kökünü `.git` arayarak buluyor. Klasörde `.git` yoksa konuşma dökümü başka bir depoya — geçmişte **public olan cloud deposuna** — yazılıyor. Yeni projenin konuşmaları oraya düşsün istemezsin.

Aynı gerekçeyle `.gitignore`'a `.env` satırını baştan koydum: bu projede daha önce gerçek bir API anahtarı yanlışlıkla public depoya girmişti, o dersi yeni depoya taşımak bedava.

Oluşan durum:

```
C:\Users\orcns\projects\vpn\    .git (dal: main), .gitignore, ilk commit 0da47a4
C:\Users\orcns\Desktop\Claude - vpn.bat
```

`CLAUDE.md` yazmadım — fikir netleşmeden yazılacak bir şey yok, diğer yeni projede de aynı şekilde bekletilmiş. VPN projesinin ne olacağını anlatırsan ilk oturumda onu birlikte kurarız.
